name: Cursor
tagline: AI-first code editor with agents, composer, and model routing

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Pro listed at $20/month, with India-only Start plan also reported separately.
pricing.freeTier: The free Hobby plan includes limited agent requests; no credit card needed.

tiers.name: Hobby
tiers.limits: Limited Agent, Chat and Tab usage with Auto; the current numeric request cap is not published.

tiers.name: Start (India)
tiers.limits: India-only entry plan; exact Agent and model-usage caps were not published on the public page.
tiers.notes: Vendor price is ₹649/month, converted at the ECB 2026-08-10 EUR/USD and EUR/INR reference cross-rate; approximately $6.81.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: $20/month of included third-party 'Other Models' usage; extended Agent limits.
tiers.notes: Annual effective price is shown by Cursor's yearly toggle.

tiers.name: Pro+
tiers.limits: $70/month of included Other Models usage and 3× Pro Agent limits.
tiers.notes: Annual effective price is shown by Cursor's yearly toggle.

tiers.name: Ultra
tiers.limits: $400/month of included Other Models usage and 20× Pro Agent limits.
tiers.notes: Annual effective price is shown by Cursor's yearly toggle.

tiers.name: Teams Standard
tiers.limits: 1 paid editor seat; Standard team Agent allowance; SAML/OIDC SSO and centralized billing.
tiers.notes: Unpaid Admin seats can administer a team but do not receive editor access.

tiers.name: Teams Premium
tiers.limits: 1 paid editor seat; 5× Teams Standard Agent allowance.
tiers.notes: Unpaid Admin seats can administer a team but do not receive editor access.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom seats and pooled usage; numeric limits and price are not public.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Hobby is free, but Cursor publishes no numeric request allowance; it only says Agent, Chat and Tab usage is limited.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual for self-serve plans; Start is monthly-only in India; taxes excluded
pricing.hiddenCosts: Usage is split into included pools that reset monthly without rollover; on-demand third-party model usage is billed in arrears at model/API rates. Cursor Router Cost mode is $1.25/M input tokens, $6/M output and $0.25/M cache read; Bugbot is separately usage-billed.

verdictSummary: You can assemble VS Code plus open-source agents, but Cursor's moat is editor-native agent UX, model routing, cloud agents, context handling, and rapid product iteration.
coreLoopDIY: Use VS Code/VSCodium plus an open-source agent extension, configure model APIs, index repos, and add workflows for edits/tests.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for speed: the agent is already in the editor with defaults that work.

priorArt.name: Continue
priorArt.desc: Open-source AI code assistant; closest practical DIY substitute when paired with VS Code o

alternatives.name: Cline
alternatives.desc: A code agent in your editor; the model bill is still yours.

facts.install: VS Code or JetBrains extension, or npm-installed CLI
facts.engines: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Azure, Vertex, Cerebras, Groq, Ollama, LM Studio and OpenAI-compatible endpoints
facts.dataFormat: Code stays in the working repository and task data is stored locally; prompts and selected code context go to the chosen provider unless a local backend is used
facts.gapVsPaid: It is an agent layered into an existing IDE rather than a cohesive AI-native editor, so autocomplete, indexing and composer-style interaction feel less integrated than Cursor.
facts.setupBlocker: Sign in for Cline inference, bring an API key, or run and configure a local model

alternatives.name: Goose
alternatives.desc: A desktop agent that edits and runs code without pretending the model is free.

facts.engines: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, Bedrock and other providers; ACP can use supported model subscriptions
facts.dataFormat: Code and files stay local; sessions and configuration are stored in Goose application data, while prompts and context go to the selected provider unless local
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a desktop or terminal agent, not a full editor with Cursor's fast tab completion, code navigation and integrated composer.
facts.setupBlocker: A provider subscription, API key or local model must be connected before the agent can work

alternatives.name: Kilo Code
alternatives.desc: One open agent across VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal; inference still has a meter somewhere.

alternatives.name: OpenCode
alternatives.desc: A fast local coding agent with no loyalty to any model vendor.

facts.engines: Dozens of providers through AI SDK and Models.dev, including hosted APIs and local OpenAI-compatible or Ollama-style backends
facts.dataFormat: Source files stay local; credentials are stored under the user's OpenCode data directory and configuration under the config directory, while prompts and context go to the selected provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It is terminal-first and does not replace Cursor's full graphical editor, low-latency autocomplete and inline review experience.
facts.setupBlocker: Terminal comfort and a provider API key or local model server are required

alternatives.name: Zed
alternatives.desc: A fast open editor with agents built in, not a VS Code costume.

facts.install: Direct desktop download, Homebrew, winget or install script
facts.engines: Zed-hosted models, provider API keys or subscriptions, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Bedrock, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible local servers and external ACP agents
facts.dataFormat: Source files stay local; provider keys use the system keychain, while AI prompts and code context go to the selected provider or local model
facts.gapVsPaid: It requires changing editors and still has a smaller extension ecosystem and less mature AI autocomplete and indexing workflow than Cursor.
facts.setupBlocker: Editor installation is clean; AI needs a Zed account, provider subscription or key, gateway, or local model, and platform hardware support varies

rejectedAlternatives.name: Continue
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Acquired by Cursor; the repo is read-only and 2.0.0 is the last release.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Refact

rejectedAlternatives.name: Roo Code
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The extension shut down and the repo was archived on May 15, 2026.

notes: A core page for a vibecoding site; the answer should not be a lazy no or yes.
prompt:
Build me an AI coding setup to replace Cursor, assembled from parts I own.
Requirements:

- Do not write an editor or an agent. Install and wire together: VS Code or
  VSCodium, the Continue extension for in-editor chat, edit, and
  autocomplete, and a terminal agent (aider or Claude Code) for multi-file
  jobs.
- Continue config at ~/.continue/config.yaml: chat and edit on Claude
  Sonnet, autocomplete on a cheap fast model (Codestral, or qwen2.5-coder
  via Ollama to keep completions local and free).
- All API keys read from environment variables set in my shell profile,
  nothing hardcoded in any config file.
- Enable Continue's codebase indexing on my main repo and verify a
  where-is-this-defined question retrieves the right file.
- Keybindings mapped to muscle memory: cmd+K edit selection, cmd+L chat,
  Tab accepts completions.
- A spend check in the README: per-token API pricing vs the $20 flat fee,
  and a reminder to compare the provider dashboards after two weeks of real
  use.
- Out of scope: cloud and background agents, Cursor's composer UX, and team
  features; that iteration speed is exactly what the subscription buys.
- README: install commands per OS, the full config file, and how to swap
  models later.
